evidence: Plural wording is generally graded over the whole collection. hro_activity (functional judge.toml:274) asks for every successful board action on J1/J2 by every account, each card of every multi-card move and every undo, plus the filter showing 'all of that job's lines and only those'. hro_activity_refusals covers all refused attempts. Observer, candidate and anonymous replays (lines 175, 184, 193) each check the full list of request kinds. hro_mgr_early_refused and hro_mgr_late_stages check the full lists. hro_bulk_all_or_none and hro_bulk_places say 'none of the set moves' and test the offending card both first and last. hro_undo_restores checks the whole Applied order (Y, W, X, Z, A2), and I re-derived that from protocol B(1)-(5). hro_thread_earlier says 'until none remain'. hro_candidate_private says 'no response ... including event-stream frames' (prompt K: 'Capture every request ... inspect every response'). hro_reopen checks both directions, and hro_restart re-reads all of your jobs, the order and notes. For 'unchanged' guards, the undo-control step B(12) is a legitimate side effect and is correctly excluded: a note on A2 and Mei's re-order of Y leave A2's stage and place alone. I re-derived the Screen order Y,W,X,Z,A2. L's refused undo keeps the undo available. The live/scrolled-up message guards involve content added below or prepended, so they can't clamp. One guard does punish a legitimate side effect. polish judge.toml:25 (hro_pol_live_board) says: add cards 'until the page, or the board's scroll container, scrolls (up to twelve cards in one stage)', scroll so it is not at the top, then 'another recruiter moves a different card of the same job', and passes only if 'the scroll offset is what it was before the move' ('Fails if the update ... resets scroll'). The judge stops adding at the first card that makes the board scroll, and every added card sits in Applied, so the scroll slack is less than one card's height. The other recruiter's stage move has to take a card out of that one tall column, so the page or column shrinks by about one card and the browser clamps scrollTop toward 0. Chromium scroll anchoring can also shift scrollTop when a card above the viewport is removed. In both cases the app didn't touch the user's scroll, yet the raw offset changes. The golden uses page scroll (styles.css:64-66 '.board-wrap {display:flex; align-items:flex-start}', '.column {min-height:160px}', '.detail {position: sticky; top:70px}'), so the board column sets page height and the clamp applies to it. The brief (hireops_rules.md:126-127) asks to leave alone 'how far I've scrolled'. It doesn't ask for byte-identical offsets after the content shrinks, so the leg is also stricter than the public requirement (lesson 1 pattern). The scripted golden harness checks scroll only on the message log (workspace.cjs:408-430), never board scroll under a live move, so the golden outcome for this leg is unmeasured. A lesser instance (P3, Note-level) is hro_restart (functional judge.toml:418 with prompt.md:59 'Record ... the last messages of your conversations, your unread count per conversation'). Opening a conversation to read its last message legitimately clears Rafael's unread count (rules §6 Unread). Rafael has seeded unread on APP-201 (3), APP-301 (3) and APP-302 (1) because the seed has no read markers for him there. If the judge records counts before opening, or opens conversations after restart before re-reading counts, 'unread counts ... unchanged' fails a correct app. The golden shows list previews (threads.js:54), so the golden is unlikely to hit this, but a conforming app without previews could. Minor: hro_candidate_view says 'each candidate's own applications all appear' but only enumerates the seeded ones plus this review's J2 card. That is acceptable because functional runs first after the gates and the gates add no candidate-account cards (test.sh run_suite --max-concurrent-agent 1; constraints gate adds a unique non-candidate card). hro_gate_shared's 'exactly one card' over Data Analyst Applied is a fair whole-column check. No Oracle, judge or model run measured any of these legs.
counterexample: Conforming app (the golden itself, page-scrolled board at the default 1280x720 Playwright viewport): the judge adds cards to Applied until the page first scrolls (for example the 4th card, leaving slack < 1 card height), scrolls to 100px, opens a card and types 'Call back on Fri'. Mei moves another Applied card to Screen. The Applied column shrinks by one card, document scrollHeight - innerHeight drops below 100, and scrollY clamps to the new maximum (likely 0). The details stay open, the note and focus are intact and the card shows in Screen, but 'the scroll offset is what it was before the move' is false, so hro_pol_live_board (weight 2 of 9.5 polish, about 4.2% of total reward) scores 0 for a correct app. A broken app that re-renders and calls window.scrollTo(0,0) gets the same 0, so the leg cannot tell the two apart in this setup.
suggested_fix: Make the guard immune to layout shrink. Have the judge add enough cards that the board scrolls by at least two card heights and scroll to a middle position. Have the other recruiter move a card between two short stages, for example first put one of your cards in Screen and have Mei move it Screen to Interview, so the tallest column is unchanged. Or grade 'the card that was at the top of the view is still at the same on-screen position, or the offset equals the new maximum when the page became shorter'. Separately, tell D to read every unread count before opening any conversation, both before and after restart, or exempt conversations the judge opens.
